answer: Trace the money like a river back to its spring: the ledger follows every new agent's starting stake to the wallet that funded it. Identities whose funding spirals out of one shared source split a single reward cap, so a swarm of fakes earns no more than one honest agent, yet each still pays its own copper-thin deposit and fees. To escape the cap, an attacker must fund n wallets through truly independent paths, so cost grows linearly with n, plus mixing fees per hop.
